title: Campaign Orbit and Close Plan Workshop
summary: Joint workshop to align on co-sell campaign structure, close plan milestones, technical POC scope, and partner attribution. Main blockers: margin splits, procurement timeline, and SOC2 clarifications. Agreed next steps include a joint close plan deck, technical checklist, and an executive alignment call.
topics: technical integration checklist (VPC, KV cache, latency)
action_items: Maya — finalize joint close plan deck and send to PulseStream by 2026-08-14
Luca — run performance delta spreadsheet against PulseStream sample data and share by 2026-08-16
Hannah — provide top 5 target accounts and champion contact info by 2026-08-13
Priya — confirm internal security reviewers and share SOC2 / ISO pack by 2026-08-15
next_steps: Share technical integration checklist and sample benchmarking template (Luca)
Initiate legal/pricing discussion after exec alignment
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-08-12
Time: 16:00 PDT
Duration: ~42 minutes
Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Luca (Redwood SE), Hannah (PulseStream Head of Partnerships), Omar (VP Sales), Priya (CTO)

Summary: quick workshop to map a joint campaign, clarify who will own which stages of the close, and lock down POC scope and success metrics.

[00:00] Maya: Hey everyone thanks for hopping on, appreciate it. Quick roll call?
[00:06] Hannah: Hi, Hannah here.
[00:08] Omar: Omar on for PulseStream.
[00:10] Priya: Priya, CTO.
[00:12] Luca: Luca from Redwood, hi all.
[00:14] Maya: Cool. The goal today is pretty pragmatic — leave with a joint close plan, a POC scope, and a set of owners. We'll also identify any procurement or security blockers early.

[00:30] Omar: Sounds good. On our side key thing is attribution. We sold last year with Synap— SynapseCloud and there was a tangle on crediting which slowed the deal. We want clear rules up front.
[00:42] Maya: Totally. We can map stages: lead, qualified, technical validation, commercial exec sign-off. We usually propose co-sell credit at legal signature unless there's a mid-stage MQL conversion that your team owns. But we're flexible.
[01:05] Hannah: Can you run through the close plan template?
[01:09] Maya: Yep — I'll share the deck after this but high level: 1) Target accounts + champions, 2) Key milestones and owners, 3) Risk register, 4) Commercial terms and margin expectations, 5) Exec alignment calendar.

[01:30] Priya: From an engineering POV the POC needs to show production-like perf. We run 95th percentile latency expectations — <350ms ideally — and we have cost guardrails. Also need to know network setup — V P C peering or private link?
[01:52] Luca: For the POC we can support both. Typically for a 30-day pilot we recommend Redwood Dedicated in one of our AZs for consistent throughput; option B is the private V P C deploy if you need data isolation. There was a small typo in the doc we sent — it said "Redwood Dedicate" — sorry about that.
[02:12] Priya: Right, the Dedicated option is fine but we need KMS/HSM integration for keys. Also audit logs and full session-level tracing for compliance.
[02:24] Luca: We have KMS integrations and can export detailed audit logs; I'll attach the SOC2 and ISO pack. Note that the audit export schema is slightly different depending on whether it's hosted API vs Dedicated. I'll call that out in the checklist.

[02:45] Omar: Pricing — we need to know expected blended cost so we can model margin. PulseStream typically expects a 25–30% margin for partner deals. How does Redwood think about partner discounts?
[02:58] Maya: We have partner tiers but given this is a strategic GTM motion, we can do a structured discount tied to committed throughput and a reserved capacity commitment. We should model both a conservative and upside scenario in the close plan.

[03:20] Hannah: Also, attribution in our CRM — we need to capture lead source and opportunity owner. If both teams are engaging, can we get a standard UTM pattern and co-sell tag to push into SFDC?
[03:33] Maya: Yes, we can provide a UTM schema and a campaign tag. We'll coordinate with your ops team.

[03:45] Priya: On integrations: we plan to forward embeddings and rerank calls for our search product to Redwood. The KV cache behavior is important — we can't have cold cache spikes affecting latency.
[03:58] Luca: Understood. We'll document KV cache warming strategies and can pre-warm for the POC. Note: sometimes internal notes transcribe KV cache as "K V cash" — apologies for earlier transcripts.

[04:15] Omar: What about competitive displacement? SynapseCloud is in two of our target accounts, GigaServe in one. We need playbooks — what's the typical success story?
[04:27] Maya: We usually lean on a technical delta narrative (latency, consistency, cost per 1k tokens), plus a business outcome — e.g., 20% cheaper inference at 95th percentile — and a reference deck. We'll include a win-theme slide per account.

[04:50] Hannah: Great. Let's talk timeline. Our procurement window is tight: legal review by Aug 26, exec sign-off by Sep 8 ideally. Can Redwood meet that?
[05:02] Maya: Yes, but we need the exec alignment call next week to lock commercial terms. How about Aug 18 for exec align?
[05:10] Omar: Works for me.

[05:20] Priya: On the POC data — can we use a small anonymized sample of our embedding indices? We can't share prod PII.
[05:29] Luca: Absolutely. We'll provide a benchmarking template; you can redact PII. We'll run the bench against your sample and share the spreadsheet.

[05:42] Maya: Ok so owners recap: Maya owns the close plan deck and commercial modelling; Luca owns technical checklist and benchmarking; Hannah owns target accounts and champion intros; Priya will shepherd security reviewers.

[06:00] Omar: A question on legal: do you accept our standard MSA or do we need to use Redwood's? We prefer to start with our standard but can be flexible.
[06:12] Maya: We can start from either, but for speed we suggest using our SOW template with your MSA redlines attached. Legal will do a fast pass once we have the deck and commitment.

[06:30] Hannah: One risk — attribution conflicts mid-funnel. Can we set an interim rule: whichever team owns the technical validation stage gets the sales credit if they drive the technical sign-off?
[06:42] Maya: We can codify that in the close plan, yes. We'll add a specific matrix: owner per stage + visibility requirements (weekly pipeline syncs).

[07:00] Priya: Security stuff again — SOC2 cert, encryption in transit & at rest, KMS, and audit log retention of 1 year minimum. Also need to confirm data residency for EU accounts.
[07:15] Luca: We'll attach the SOC2 package and an EU-data-residency note. For KMS we support bring-your-own-key; retention policies can be configured.

[07:35] Omar: Demo ask — can Redwood do a short 20-minute tailored demo for the execs on Aug 18? Focus on latency/SLAs and integration ease.
[07:46] Maya: Yes, we'll do a 20-minute exec-friendly demo and a technical deep dive with Priya and engineering on subsequent call.

[08:00] Hannah: Anything else?
[08:02] Maya: Quick other items: pricing bands, the pilot acceptance criteria — we'll propose p95 < 400ms, p50 < 120ms, accuracy/quality check on sampled prompts, and cost per 1k tokens target. If those are met we'll trigger a commercial proposal.

[08:25] Priya: Works. Also can we include rollback/fallback policies in case of regressions during POC?
[08:33] Luca: Yes, we'll define fallback to a smaller model variant or temporary throttling.

[08:45] Maya: Alright, recap and next steps: I'll share the joint close plan deck and calendar invite for Aug 18 exec align. Luca will send the integration checklist and benchmarking template. Hannah to send target accounts. Priya to loop in security reviewers.

[09:05] Omar: Thanks everyone.
[09:08] Maya: Thanks — will follow up with links.

References shared: Joint close plan draft: https://redwood.app/decks/joint-close-plan (draft); Tech checklist & bench template: https://redwood.app/benchmarks/pulse-template (private link)

End of transcript.
